items.title: NALSAR Convocation row: No inquiry, proceedings closed, says BCI Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra
items.summary: Bar Council of India (BCI) chairman Manan Kumar Mishra has stated that the BCI has decided to close the proceedings against graduating students at NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad who had objected to Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant attending their convocation as chief guest. Mishra said that there won't be any inquiry against the students, a departure from the BCI's earlier decision. The decision follows representations and reactions of Senior Advocates, members of the bar, law students and public spirited citizens, the BCI chairman said "After considering the representations and reactions of Senior Advocates, learned members of the Bar, law students and public spirited citizens, and being satisfied that the 2026 batch of NALSAR, Hyderabad, had no role in any disturbance or movement, the Bar Council of India has decided to close the proceedings altogether. No further action is required from NALSAR," he said. Wishing the students best for their careers, he said, "A word of wisdom: we take immense pride in our legal institutions, and the day you enrol, you become vanguards. items.title: A Fundamental Right
items.summary: With its new law that makes education a fundamental right with effect from April 1, 2010, India joins a small group of countries with such a statutory provision. All children in the 6 to 14 age group can exercise the right under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009. An estimated one crore children who do not go to school now are expected to benefit.
